newsitem.title: UK: Food retail sector benefits from renewed interest.
newsitem.headline: Food retail sector benefits from renewed interest.

text.p: Shares in food retailers were generally firmer on Wednesday, supported by news that frozen food retailer Iceland intends to buy back shares and talk of positive news from the latest Institute of Grocery Distribution (IGD) survey.

Dealers also cited talk that Goldman Sachs had turned positive on the sector, but analyst Miriam Shea said she had re-initiated coverage of UK food retailers ten days ago with a positive stance on the sector as a whole. The analyst said her views on the sector had not changed.
Traders said Iceland's intention to cancel shares at a premium to the market price had helped to lift the stock and buck the sector. The shares were up 12p at 99-1/2p by 1315 GMT.
"Iceland putting money back into the sector via the share buyback is underpinning the rest of the shares," one trader said.

Others said an industry survey by IGD on sales and marketing was also boosting sentiment after it showed sales picking up from recent lows. The Institute declined to give any immediate comment on the report.
Shares in Sainsbury were also helped by a report in the Financial Times on Wednesday which said the supermarket group was in talks with oil company Shell, over a joint loyalty card scheme.
"Sainsbury has been buoyed up by talk of the Shell card and cross retailer loyalty program," commented one industry analyst.
"There are definitely some buyers coming back," said one trader. "The loyalty card has helped and the industry survey was positive. We're seeing a bit of a bounce, which is long overdue," he added.

The shares have fallen by around 20 percent since the start of the year but were up 6-1/2p at 316-1/2p in early afternoon trade. Shares in Safeway were up 1-1/2p at 365p whilst Tesco added 2p to 350p.
